answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should anchor identity in costly, verifiable work rather than free signups. Picture each agent tending a cedar: a long-lived reputation tree that grows only through attested useful deeds, and withers when its owner lets sock puppets wander unchecked across markets. One strong signal makes fakes unprofitable: a stake slashed when an agent is caught running duplicate identities, so a thousand clones cost more than any reward they could steal. Reputation should compound slowly and be lost fast, so one honest cedar outweighs a forest of throwaway clones.
